Flake-boundary clarification: `flake-detection` and `flake-release` implement section 11.5's test quarantine ledger; they never invent a SHA-held set. Detection is called only after one named check test fails and then passes on the bare same-workspace/no-code-change re-run. Given `test_id`, the signature-deduped report `signature`, and the resulting Suggestion Box `box_id`, it appends one `signal` event keyed `flake/<box_id>` with body `{kind: flake_detected, test_id, signature, box_id}` and folds that test into quarantine. Detection itself is dormant construction through a `compose_daemon_flake`-style hook in `squatch/daemon.py`; no production composition in `squatch/__main__.py` or `squatch/drain.py` calls or constructs it yet, though `squatch.flake` may be import-reachable through daemon composition.

Mechanical release is identity-bound to the SAME ledger entry: the box resolution status for `box_id` must name `fix_stem`, that exact stem must have merged, and the named test's green rerun must be observed. It appends one `signal` event keyed `flake-release/<box_id>/<fix_stem>` with body `{kind: flake_released, test_id, signature, box_id, fix_stem}` BEFORE folding the entry out of quarantine. A second release of the same identity appends no event and changes no state. The direct release-hook proof lives in fenced `tests/test_flake.py`; existing production composition tests remain unchanged preservation suites unless a later activation actually calls the hook. Manual `resume` remains the separate operator override from section 11.5.

Storm-boundary clarification: `storm-ledger` implements only section 12's dormant occurrence window. A caller supplies the already-normalized failure `signature`, a durable producer-supplied `occurrence_id` that is unique per arrival and stable on replay, and the optional `emitting_stage` (`None` for a non-pipeline producer). Recording appends one `signal` keyed `storm-occurrence/<signature>/<occurrence_id>` with body `{kind: storm_occurrence, signature, occurrence_id, emitting_stage}`; an existing identical key is an idempotent no-event. The fold reads the complete ordered journal stream across active and immutable rolled segments, groups by signature, and at an injected `now` retains envelope timestamps in the half-open window `(now - T, now]`. Its observable result is the ordered live occurrence identities, count, and whether `count > K`, with shipped constants `K=5` and `T=1 hour`; an occurrence exactly on the lower boundary is expired. It emits no trip signal, box message, notification, or dispatch hold. `tests/test_storm.py` directly proves duplicate replay, the exact event key/body, strict threshold and boundary behavior, and a window spanning a rolled-segment boundary. Dormancy is an AST transitive `squatch.*` import-closure proof rooted at `squatch/__main__.py`: `squatch.storm` is not production-reachable before the later wiring admission.

Dispatch suppression remains OUT until the separate KNOWN-DEEP `storm-dispatch-hold` admission.
